To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

online communities for d/deaf and hard of Hearing are mostly established and maintained by institutions, organizations, or associations and that they are used to support d/ Deaf and hard of hearin in their everyday life, education, and professional life.

the majority of online communities for the d/Deaf in Germany are organized and run by institutions, organizations and associations, that they support d/Deafs in their personal, educational and working life and that their content is mostly written and signed language.

Facebook communities for the d/Deaf are mostly initiated by institutions and associations, that communication between community members takes place mostly in sign language, and that the feature of posting video comments is not technically available.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of online communities and the way they are used to support the d/Deaf community.
the question whether online communities for d/deaf and hard of the hearing people are a useful tool for supporting d/Deaf community members in their everyday life.
how online communities for d/deaf and hard of people operate and how they support the needs of their members in the online environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
online communities for d/Dear and hard of hearing are still in their early stages of development.
online communities for d/deaf and hard of the hearing are not a replacement for offline communities but rather an extension.
the analyzed online communities are a part of the d/Deaf community, but not the community itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Facebook is not a suitable tool for d/Deafs to create a community by themselves, but it can be used to support the activities of existing offline communities.
the use of online communities by d/Deaf users in the context of social media is still limited, and the technical features of online communities are not fully exploited.
Facebook communities for the d/Deaf have not yet reached the level where they can be considered as an autonomous and self-determined online community.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the online communities for the d/Deaf community are still not fully utilized in terms of the potential of online communities.
the accessibility of communities is not guaranteed and that the accessibility of online communities for people with hearing disabilities is not yet a priority for community developers.
the accessibility of online communities for the deaf and hard of hearing is still a problem, and it needs to be solved by the administrators of online communities.
